title: Connecting an app again keeps the running app signed in until it collects its new credentials, Lys hands an app its own public address, reads the app's manifest itself, and knows which apps connected by themselves
purpose: The 18 October 2026 surface review's apps domain (builder 04, lys-review/CONSENSUS.md, Server asks) left four things the screens cannot do because the server does not: its own worst case is that connecting an approved app again revokes the running app's credentials at Approve (apps_connect.rs at ca1228b0: connect, line 275, calls replace_credentials at 353 and then revokes every entry of record.prior at 355), before the app has exchanged its new code, so a reconnect the app never finishes cuts every clinician's sign-in to it until someone finishes the connect on the app's side; the surface now warns before Approve, which is a floor. The approve page hands the app the browser's own origin as Lys's address, so an administrator at localhost hands Cambium an address Cambium cannot dial; the server already computes the dialable address for runners (network_join/routes.rs dial_address). The approve page reads the app's manifest from the browser, so a browser rule (CORS, mixed content) and a dead app look the same and the page can only say it cannot tell which. And Lys's surface carries a list of known app names (ConnectApp.tsx KNOWN_APPS) against ADR-116, because the server does not say which apps connected by themselves or from where.
task: In lys-identity-server: move the revocation of an app's prior credentials from connect to the exchange, after the new values are handed over; add public_address and connect_origin to GET /apps; add GET /apps/connect/manifest?address= that reads a manifest server-side for an administrator and answers it or a named reason. In the surface: the approve page sends public_address and shows it, reads the manifest through the server, drops KNOWN_APPS and offers Connect again from each app's own card with its connect_origin, and keys "given its credentials by connecting" on connect_origin. apps_api.rs is 631 lines at ca1228b0; the GET /apps answer builder moves to apps_api_read.rs first, as a move with no change, so each file is under 500 (ADR-111). Out of scope: the app-side registration itself (DIRECTORY-059 R5 specifies POST /apps/connect-requests; this brief only orders it first and names its origin).

requirements.title: Prior credentials are revoked after the exchange, not at Approve
requirements.spec: Behavioural. In crates/lys-identity-server/src/apps_connect.rs, connect no longer revokes record.prior after replace_credentials; the entries stay in record.prior, marked with the operation that replaced them. exchange (line 423 at ca1228b0), after it has handed the new values to the app's server and the hand-over is recorded, revokes every prior credential that operation replaced, with the reason "the app was connected again". A reconnect the app never finishes therefore leaves the running app signed in with its old credentials; a second reconnect before the first exchange replaces the pending values and keeps the same prior set. The approve page's words (surface/identity/src/features/apps/ConnectApp.tsx) change from the warning and "Approve and replace its credentials" to "Approve" with the line "The running app keeps its credentials until it collects the new ones."
acceptance: Red first: a test in crates/lys-identity-server/src/apps_connect_reconnect_tests.rs connects an approved app again, reads that the prior credential still authenticates after Approve, exchanges, and reads that it is refused after the exchange with the reason named
A second connect before any exchange, then one exchange, revokes the first prior set once and leaves nothing live but the newest values
The approve page's vitest case shows the new words and no warning

requirements.title: GET /apps answers Lys's own public address for an app to dial
requirements.spec: Behavioural. GET /apps gains public_address: string | null, computed as network_join/routes.rs dial_address(state.oidc.redirect_url()) computes it for runners, and null with a public_address_reason naming why (loopback, plain http) when that refuses. The GET /apps answer builder moves from apps_api.rs to apps_api_read.rs first, unchanged, so both files are under 500 lines. The approve page (ConnectApp.tsx, KnownAppRow and the connect-again act) sends lys=<public_address> to the app instead of the browser's origin and shows it in its "<app> will call Lys back at" line; when it is null the page says the reason and that the app will be handed the browser's address, and names what to change (the registered address) to fix it.
acceptance: Red first: a test in crates/lys-identity-server/src/apps_api_read_tests.rs reads public_address equal to dial_address's answer for a registered https address, and null with a reason for a loopback one
The approve page's vitest cases show the address sent and shown, and the reason line when null
apps_api.rs and apps_api_read.rs are each under 500 lines

requirements.title: Lys reads an app's manifest itself for the approve page
requirements.spec: Behavioural. GET /apps/connect/manifest?address=<manifest url>, administrator only, fetches the manifest from Lys's server and answers it, or one named reason: not answering (with the connection error's words), answered with a status (the status), or not a manifest (what was found). No browser rule stands between the approve page and the app. ConnectApp.tsx reads this route instead of fetch(manifestUrl); its two-cause sentence ("cannot tell whether Cambium is not answering there or does not let this Lys read it") and the Open-the-manifest link go, and each named reason is said as its own line with the next act. surface/identity/tests/apps-connect.test.tsx and src/features/apps/connect-manifest.test.tsx pin the three reasons and the manifest case.
acceptance: Red first: a test in crates/lys-identity-server/src/apps_connect_manifest_tests.rs serves a manifest, a 503, and an HTML page from a fixture app and reads the manifest and the two reasons; a non-administrator is refused
The approve page's vitest cases show the manifest's app name on success and one reason line per failure, with no two-cause sentence left (grep of ConnectApp.tsx for "cannot tell" answers 0)

requirements.title: Lys knows which apps connected by themselves and from where; the surface holds no app's name
requirements.spec: Behavioural. Each app in GET /apps gains connect_origin: string | null, the origin of the manifest it last connected with, null for an app registered by hand. The app-side registration of DIRECTORY-059 R5 (POST /apps/connect-requests) is the first step of a connect: an app that registered itself is listed on Apps as pending under its own name before anyone types its address. ConnectApp.tsx drops KNOWN_APPS: the Connect card offers "Another app" by address only; each connected app's own card offers Connect again with its connect_origin filled in; and the "given its credentials by connecting" marking keys on connect_origin !== null instead of the name list, so no app name lives in Lys's code (ADR-116).
acceptance: Red first: a test in apps_api_read_tests.rs reads connect_origin for an app that connected by manifest and null for one registered by hand
grep of surface/identity/src for KNOWN_APPS answers 0 after the change, and the Apps vitest cases show a self-registered app pending under its own name and Connect again on a connected app's card

boundaries: SHALL NOT revoke any credential before the exchange that replaces it has handed the new values over.
SHALL NOT keep an app's name in the surface's or the server's code (ADR-116).
SHALL NOT read a manifest for anyone but an administrator, and SHALL NOT follow a manifest address to a loopback or private address of Lys's own host.
SHALL NOT put a fixed wait, deadline or poll anywhere, in code or test.
SHALL NOT leave apps_api.rs over 500 lines: the move to apps_api_read.rs comes first, unchanged.
verification: Red first for every requirement; cargo nextest run only (never cargo test), clippy pedantic -D warnings, cargo fmt; vitest and tsc for the surface files; the design gate's validate.py and check-coverage.py on the cluster parsed for FAIL lines, never by exit code; file length 500 on every file touched.

Done means: every route and field answers as specified with the named tests green on the Mac, the surface reads each one, the openapi contract test is green, and the lane's END names any file it touched beyond the lists here so the brief is amended in one commit.
